record_identity.title: Work Is Not Delivered Until It Can Survive Interruption

report_title: Work Is Not Delivered Until It Can Survive Interruption
case_descriptor: Lessons from substantive coding-agent work lost before durable persistence
summary: Agent work is not operationally complete while its only usable state remains ephemeral, session-bound, quota-dependent, or inaccessible. Reliable execution requires proportionate checkpointing, truthful delivery posture, safe interruption handling, and a recovery artefact sufficient for resumption, inspection, transfer, rollback, or manual completion.
what_happened: On 11 June 2026, a quota-limited Codex cloud task performed substantive repository work but exhausted the available allowance before establishing a durable branch, commit, patch, or equivalent recovery artefact.
The task later failed and the completed work was unavailable, requiring duplicate execution and additional user quota.
CAM adopted durable work-state, safe-pause, checkpoint-record, delivery-posture, and infrastructure-continuity controls without guaranteeing that every downstream action will succeed.
governance_misconception: Substantive processing was treated as task completion even though the work product remained inaccessible and non-recoverable.
Branch creation, pull-request creation, or final publication was treated as the first meaningful persistence boundary rather than one of several possible handoff steps.
Quota, session, authentication, network, device, tool, and infrastructure limits were treated as external inconveniences rather than foreseeable execution-continuity conditions.
abstracted_learning: Completion, persistence, and delivery are different states. A long-running or materially consequential agent must preserve enough durable state before interruption risk becomes material, and must represent honestly whether work is processing, checkpointed, resumable, substantively complete but undelivered, durably delivered, or failed with recoverable state.
integrated_learning: Substantive work is not durably delivered merely because the agent has finished reasoning or modification.
Checkpointing should be proportionate to duration, cost, mutation depth, and interruption risk.
A pull request is neither the first nor the only valid persistence boundary.
Safe pause should occur at an atomic boundary that avoids corrupting files, transactions, repositories, or external state.
When interruption risk becomes material, preserving recoverable state should take priority over optional packaging, polish, publication, or administration.
Temporary preservation does not create user approval, merge authority, deployment authority, or final adoption.
risk_if_not_integrated: Completed work may disappear after quota exhaustion, timeout, authentication loss, tool failure, or session termination.
Users may be forced to repeat paid or quota-consuming work and bear avoidable delay, cost, and cognitive burden.
Systems may misrepresent ephemeral processing as completion and conceal that no usable deliverable exists.
Unsafe interruption may corrupt repositories, files, transactions, audit lineage, or external state.
Teams may be unable to inspect, transfer, resume, roll back, or manually complete material work.
generalisation_boundary: This lesson does not require continuous persistence of every transient thought, guarantee successful pull-request creation or publication, or prohibit temporary execution environments. It applies where the work is materially consequential and foreseeable interruption could make completed work inaccessible, non-reconstructable, or falsely represented as delivered.
